{
  "need": "Identity",
  "secondary": { "name": "Belonging" },
  "read": "Your kid is trying to figure out who they are and whether their family's values are real or just rules imposed on them. When they asked that hard question, they were reaching toward you — testing whether you're a person they can actually learn from, or just an authority figure giving rehearsed answers. The freeze probably landed as a wall, and now they may be wondering if honesty only flows one direction in this house.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Protector", "instinct": "Never bring it up again and hope they forget — which protects you from the discomfort but teaches them that vulnerability and honesty are for everyone except the adults in charge, and quietly kills the trust you need for every harder conversation ahead." },
  "mentorMove": "Go back to them yourself, before they have to ask again. Sitting with the discomfort of being honest about your past is exactly how you show them that the standard — being real with people who love you — applies to you too, not just to them.",
  "holdFirm": ["You owe them a real answer, or at least a real explanation of why you're not ready yet — silence is not a neutral choice here.", "The expectation that your family talks honestly with each other has to include you; you can't hold them to openness you won't model."],
  "stayFlexible": ["You get to decide how much detail is appropriate for their age — you don't have to hand over every corner of your past, just enough honesty to be a real person to them.", "You can name what made you freeze — 'that question caught me off guard and I wasn't sure how to answer it well' — without having the whole conversation figured out before you start."],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 1, "label": "Empathy" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, I've been thinking about the other day when you asked me that question and I just kind of went blank on you. I didn't want to leave it like that." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "Can I ask what made you bring that up? I want to make sure I actually answer what you were really asking, not just what I assumed you meant." },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here's the honest truth: I froze because I didn't have a clean answer, and part of me didn't want to say something that came out wrong. But I also know that me going silent wasn't fair to you — you asked a real question and you deserved a real response. So here's what I can actually tell you..." },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I expect you to be straight with me when things get hard, and I hold myself to the same thing — that's not a rule I get to skip because it's uncomfortable. I know you can handle the real me, and I want you to know you can always come back with the hard questions." }
  ],
  "longGame": "Every time you go back and repair an awkward moment like this one, you're building the exact relationship where they'll come to you when things are actually serious — not because you were perfect, but because they've seen that you show up even when it costs you something."
}
situation: My teenager asked me a hard question about something I did at their age, and I froze instead of answering.
